objective: Assess whether Project SkyNet should launch urban drone delivery based on financial viability, consumer acceptance, UAM corridor compliance, and fleet readiness (Heavy-Lifter v2 vs. Swift-Class).
decision_question: Should OmniLogistics proceed with the urban launch of Project SkyNet given the regulatory compliance issues with Heavy-Lifter v2, consumer acceptance levels, and financial projections?

Financial Viability.Capital Expenditure: $45.5M allocated; break-even at 18 months with 150k daily packages
Financial Viability.Cost Reduction: Projected 35% reduction in last-mile delivery cost ($4.10 to $2.66) by Q4 2027

Consumer Acceptance.Overall Comfort: 68% comfortable; 55% willing to pay up to $2.50 premium for 30-min delivery

Regulatory Compliance.Altitude Limits: 150-300 ft cruising; below 150 ft only during VTOL
Regulatory Compliance.Restricted Zones: No flights over schools during hours, major sporting events, government buildings
Regulatory Compliance.Weight Limits: Max 25 lbs for unrestricted corridor access; Heavy-Lifter v2 exceeds by 2.5 lbs
Regulatory Compliance.Data Retention: 90 days minimum for telemetry and sensor data

Fleet Readiness.Heavy-Lifter v2: Total weight 27.5 lbs (exceeds 25 lbs limit); non-compliant for urban corridors
Fleet Readiness.Swift-Class: Total weight 18 lbs; compliant; recommended for urban centers

hypotheses.hypothesis: H1: Financial viability is strong if Swift-Class drones are used, as they comply with weight limits and can achieve the projected delivery volumes.
H2: Consumer acceptance is sufficient (68% comfortable) but requires mitigation of noise and privacy concerns via Whisper-Prop and camera shuttering.
H3: Heavy-Lifter v2 cannot be used in urban corridors due to weight non-compliance; fleet mix must prioritize Swift-Class.
H4: Regulatory compliance is achievable with Swift-Class drones, but operational adjustments (e.g., route planning to avoid restricted zones) are needed.
